name: Taj Mahal

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/375257537 (centre of the tomb on its plinth: middle of the outline, 0.9 m west and 0.15 m north of its centroid; heading = the south front towards the great gate, from the same outline, 179.9°)

rights.note: Built for Shah Jahan to the design attributed to Ustad Ahmad Lahori: the tomb 1632–1643, the mosque, jawab, garden and gate finished c. 1653. Every author died centuries ago.

Taj Mahal — Wikipedia (en): total height 73 m, plinth 6 m high and 95.5 m square, pishtaqs 33 m, drum 12 m (inner diameter 18.4 m), dome 23 m, finial 9.6 m, minarets over 40 m in three parts, terrace 300 m long and 8.7 m high

Origins and architecture of the Taj Mahal — Wikipedia (en), after Ebba Koch, «The Complete Taj Mahal» (2006): tomb 56.9 m square, drum about 7 m visible, minaret 43.02 m, terrace 300 × 111.89 m, charbagh 296.31 m square, mosque 56.6 × 23.38 × 20.3 m, great gate 41.2 × 34 × 23.07 m
SRTM and ASTER 30 m elevation, via OpenTopoData: the garden ≈ 162 m, the river bank ≈ 148–153 m

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q9141_taj_mahal.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The tomb with its plinth, iwans, niches, pinnacles, drum, onion dome, lotus crown and gilded finial with crescent, the four chhatris and the four minarets; the red sandstone terrace on the river with its octagonal towers; the mosque (west) and the jawab (east) with three white domes, corner towers and their tanks; the charbagh with the raised marble channels, the fountain jets, the central tank (al-Hawd al-Kawthar), cypress rows, sixteen sunken beds with trees, the pavilions of the cross axis, the crenellated walls with corner towers and the great gate (Darwaza-i rauza) with its rows of eleven chhatris. Heights from Koch / Wikipedia; estimated (±15–30 %): terrace 1.2 m above the garden, the side parapets of the tomb (24 m above the plinth; the 33 m of the pishtaqs taken from the terrace, as the OSM parts give), the bulb (27.4 m across on a 23 m drum), the chhatris, the mosque domes and their heights, walls 7 m, towers, pavilions and the gate's towers. OpenStreetMap draws the garden, its channels and the gate about 9 m east of the axis of the tomb, mosque and terrace; they were put back on the axis and made symmetric, with the south wall 296.3 m from the terrace (Koch). The minarets' slight outward lean, the inlay and carving, the forecourt (jilaukhana) south of the gate and the Mehtab Bagh are left out. y = 0 is the garden walks; the terrace is at +1.2 and its river face goes down to −10.
